title: Gérard Fiou Sancerre Rouge “Terroir Silex”
about: Domaine Gérard Fiou is a small family estate based in the village of Saint-Satur, on the eastern side of the Sancerre appellation, facing Pouilly-Fumé across the Loire. Gérard’s grandfather was both a vine-grower and a cooper; Gérard himself concentrated on the vineyards. According to the Guide Hachette, the domaine has been part of the Sancerre house of Henri Bourgeois since 2010. It is one of only a handful of producers on this side of the appellation.

Saint-Satur’s slopes are rich in silex, or flint, a soil the importer says covers only about 15% of the appellation and which gives the domaine its name for mineral wines; the estate’s vines average around 60 years old. For this red, Pinot Noir grows on clay and silica soils facing south-west. The wine is fermented in temperature-controlled stainless steel, goes through malolactic fermentation and is then aged for six months in oak barrels. The importer reports the estate as certified organic from the 2023 vintage.

Sancerre is best known for Sauvignon Blanc, but red Sancerre is always Pinot Noir, grown here at the cool northern edge of red-wine country. Tasters on Delectable describe a markedly mineral nose with dark berry fruit, a wilder, musky note and chalky tannins, and one called it unlike any other Sancerre rouge they had tried. It suits duck, game birds, mushrooms and soft cheeses. The importer does not publish an alcohol level for this cuvée.
facts: Dry red, six months in barrel
